`agent-files version` prints the set version, the name of the `agent-data/agent-files-vX.Y.Z`
file with its prefix removed, bare, one per line when a bump left several, and fails outside a
workspace or in one without the file.

`agent-files diff [A] [B]` compares two copies of the set, one line per file, names only: `same`,
`differs`, `only in A`, or `only in B`, then `N of M differ`. It answers whether a re-sync is a
copy, and its exit status is non-zero when anything differs, as `diff`'s is. `custom.md` is
reported as the project layer and not compared unless `-c`/`--custom` compares it like the rest,
for a family whose project layers are meant to be identical, and `--no-custom` overrides a config
that says so.

`A` is the operand, else the config's `agent-files.diff.dir`, else `family.template`, the config
values relative to the config file's directory. `B` is the operand, else this workspace. So a
bare `diff` compares the payload against this workspace, one operand compares that copy against
this workspace, and two operands compare any two copies from anywhere, no workspace needed. The
header line says where each came from, and a missing or non-directory operand is an error naming
what to set.

`agent-files copy [SRC] [DST]` makes the set in `DST` a byte copy of the one in `SRC`: it copies
what differs or exists only in `SRC`, deletes what exists only in `DST` under `agent-data/`,
never touches `TODO.md`, and copies `custom.md` only with `-c`/`--custom`. The operands resolve
as `diff`'s do: `SRC` is the operand, else `agent-files.copy.dir`, else `family.template`, and
`DST` is the operand, else this workspace. So a bare `copy` re-syncs this workspace from the
payload, and two operands copy between any two directories, which is how a maintainer folds an
adopter's set into the payload. It prints its source and destination and each step first,
refuses a `DST` whose jj working copy already changes a set file, so the copy's changes are the
only ones there, and leaves the result uncommitted: `jj diff` there is the review, and the
commit is yours to make. A `DST` outside any jj repo gets no guard, and the run says so.

`agent-files size [DIR]` counts the set's markdown, `AGENTS.md`, `custom.md`, and
`agent-data/*.md`, one line per file and a total. The version marker has no `.md` extension, so it
takes no row and no place in the file count, and being empty it would add nothing to the total
either. `agent-data/rationale.md` is counted: its number is shown in angle brackets and left out
of the total, being the rules' why rather than a rule, so a rule gaining a why does not read as
the set growing.

It then slides the per-file table in `notes/agent-files-size.md`, the one headed `| File |`: a new
leftmost column labelled by the set's version file goes in, the rightmost column goes out, and the
window keeps the width it had. A file new to the set takes its sorted slot with empty cells behind
it, one gone from the set keeps its remaining numbers until the window passes them, and the `total`
row stays last. It is dry-run by default, printing the table it would write, and `--no-dry-run`
applies it. `DIR` is the operand, else this workspace, `--file` names another notes file, and
`--label` names a column the version file cannot: write `--label=- v0.1.0` for a label opening on
a `-`. The `## Counts` table above is left alone, since its note is prose.

vc-x1 agent-files diff ../iiac-perf                # a peer's copy against this workspace
vc-x1 agent-files diff ../iiac-perf -c             # custom.md too
vc-x1 agent-files diff ../iiac-perf ../zc-ring-x1  # two peers, from anywhere

vc-x1 agent-files size                             # the count, and the slide it would make

for a family whose project layers are meant to be identical, and `--no-custom` overrides a config
that says so.

`A` is the operand, else the config's `agent-files.diff.dir`, else `family.template`, the config
values relative to the config file's directory. `B` is the operand, else this workspace. So a
bare `diff` compares the payload against this workspace, one operand compares that copy against
this workspace, and two operands compare any two copies from anywhere, no workspace needed. The
header line says where each came from, and a missing or non-directory operand is an error naming
what to set.

`agent-files copy [SRC] [DST]` makes the set in `DST` a byte copy of the one in `SRC`: it copies
what differs or exists only in `SRC`, deletes what exists only in `DST` under `agent-data/`,
never touches `TODO.md`, and copies `custom.md` only with `-c`/`--custom`. The operands resolve
as `diff`'s do: `SRC` is the operand, else `agent-files.copy.dir`, else `family.template`, and
`DST` is the operand, else this workspace. So a bare `copy` re-syncs this workspace from the
payload, and two operands copy between any two directories, which is how a maintainer folds an
adopter's set into the payload. It prints its source and destination and each step first,
refuses a `DST` whose jj working copy already changes a set file, so the copy's changes are the
only ones there, and leaves the result uncommitted: `jj diff` there is the review, and the
commit is yours to make. A `DST` outside any jj repo gets no guard, and the run says so.

`agent-files size [DIR]` counts the set's markdown, `AGENTS.md`, `custom.md`, and
`agent-data/*.md`, one line per file and a total. The version marker has no `.md` extension, so it
takes no row and no place in the file count, and being empty it would add nothing to the total
either. `agent-data/rationale.md` is counted: its number is shown in angle brackets and left out
of the total, being the rules' why rather than a rule, so a rule gaining a why does not read as
the set growing.

It then slides the per-file table in `notes/agent-files-size.md`, the one headed `| File |`: a new
leftmost column labelled by the set's version file goes in, the rightmost column goes out, and the
window keeps the width it had. A file new to the set takes its sorted slot with empty cells behind
it, one gone from the set keeps its remaining numbers until the window passes them, and the `total`
row stays last. It is dry-run by default, printing the table it would write, and `--no-dry-run`
applies it. `DIR` is the operand, else this workspace, `--file` names another notes file, and
`--label` names a column the version file cannot: write `--label=- v0.1.0` for a label opening on
a `-`. The `## Counts` table above is left alone, since its note is prose.

```
vc-x1 agent-files diff                             # the payload against this workspace
vc-x1 agent-files diff ../iiac-perf                # a peer's copy against this workspace
vc-x1 agent-files diff ../iiac-perf -c             # custom.md too
vc-x1 agent-files diff ../iiac-perf ../zc-ring-x1  # two peers, from anywhere
vc-x1 agent-files copy                             # re-sync this workspace from the payload
vc-x1 agent-files copy ../iiac-perf -c             # take a peer's set, custom.md included
vc-x1 agent-files copy ../iiac-perf ../vc-x1-template/work  # fold a peer's set into the payload
vc-x1 agent-files size                             # the count, and the slide it would make
vc-x1 agent-files size --no-dry-run                # slide the table
```

content.content:
assignment line ready to paste in. The schema is generated at build time from the `vc-config.md`
prototype at the repo root (see
[vc-config.md (the schema prototype)](#vc-configmd-the-schema-prototype)), so it can't drift
from what the code actually reads.

- `[TARGET]`: `work`, `agent`, `work,agent` (default), or an explicit config-file path.
  - a keyword resolves against the surrounding workspace's config files and filters to that
    side's keys: `agent` prints the `[agent-session]` and `[repos]` keys the agent repo's config
    may hold, `work` adds `[family]` and `[validate]`, and `work,agent` prints both sides, one
    block each, under a header naming the file it resolved to
  - anything else is taken as a path to a config file. A path carries no side information, so
    in print mode it gets the whole schema for every home (the user-tier keys included) with the
    path as a label, and the file is not opened. The user config (`~/.config/vc-x1/config.toml`)

- `[repos]`: the two repos' local paths, written by `init`. The one table the agent repo's config
  carries too.
- `[remote]` (0.84.12): remote names rather than paths. Its one key, `agent-repo`, is the
  agent-repo's name on its remote, which `clone` reads before there is an agent-repo to ask.
  - Only the last URL segment is recorded. The owner and the host come from the work repo's own
    remote, so the two repos are siblings in one namespace.
  - An absent key means a name derived from `repos.agent`'s last component: a dot-led one is
    appended to the work repo's name (`.claude` gives `<name>.claude`), any other is used whole.
- `[family]` (0.80.0): the agent-file family this repo belongs to, which was prose in the project
  layer before.
- `[validate]` (0.80.0): the commands that validate this repo, also prose in the project layer
  before.
- `[agent-files.diff]` and `[agent-files.copy]` (0.83.0): the defaults for the `agent-files`
  commands' `DIR` operand and `--custom` choice.

All but `[repos]` are work side only: `validate-config` reports them unknown in the agent repo's
config.

````markdown
```toml
[repos]
work = "."
agent = ".claude"                 # the agent repo's directory, relative to this file
```

```toml
[remote]
agent-repo = "vc-x1.claude"       # the agent repo's name on its remote
```

```toml
[family]
member = "vc-x1"                  # this repo's name in the family, and its messages record
template = "../vc-x1-template/work"  # the payload directory holding the pinned agent-files
messages = "../vc-x1-messages"    # the family's notification repo
```

```toml
[validate]
full = [                          # the per-commit validation, in order, one command per element
  "cargo fmt",
  "cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings",
  "cargo test",
  "cargo install --path . --locked",
]
fast = ["cargo test --bins"]      # the subset a ladder rung runs
```

```toml
[agent-files.diff]
dir = "../iiac-perf"              # default DIR for agent-files diff, else family.template
custom = true                     # compare custom.md too, as -c/--custom would

[agent-files.copy]
dir = "../vc-x1-template/work"    # default DIR for agent-files copy, else family.template
custom = false                    # never copy custom.md unless -c/--custom
```
````

The `custom` keys are `bool` keys, a bare `true` or `false`: `validate-config` reports a quoted
or other value as a finding by shape, and the commands refuse a config that holds one. A `dir`
is relative to the config file's directory, and absent, the command falls back to
`family.template`. The flags win over the table for one run: `-c`/`--custom` turns custom.md
on, `--no-custom` turns it off, and a `DIR` operand replaces `dir`.

The `[validate]` lists are `str-list` keys: a TOML array of strings, one element per invocation,
on one line or spread to the closing `]`. Each element is one command whose exit status is
checked, so a command with its own spaces and dashes is one quoted string.
[`vc-x1 validate`](#validate) (and `--fast`) runs them, `validate-config` checks the tables'
keys and shapes, and `config work` prints the schema with every key's example:

```
vc-x1 validate-config                       # both sides
vc-x1 validate-config work                  # the work side only
vc-x1 validate-config agent                 # the agent side only
vc-x1 validate-config .claude/.vc-config.md # a specific file, checked against every home
vc-x1 config work                             # the work side's schema, [family], [validate], and [agent-files.*] too
vc-x1 config agent                            # the agent side's schema
vc-x1 config .claude/.vc-config.md            # the whole schema, labelled with the path
```

### clone

Clone an existing dual-repo project. Runs `git clone --recursive` to get both repos, initializes
`jj` in each, and creates the Claude Code symlink.

What is being done: the running cycle's planning and its work's documentation. The last
finished cycle's is in [zCLOSED.md](zCLOSED.md), and what we might do is in [TODO.md](TODO.md). The

## In Progress

### feat: the family directory

(wink + agent, 2026-10-16) Each member's `.vc-config.md` names the family's shared resources, the
template's payload and the messages repo, in a `[family]` table of its own, and nothing lists the
members, so the family's shape is copied into every member and drifts as members join, which is
coming soon. The shared part of each member's `custom.md`, its Messaging and Fetch entries, is
copied the same way, with no master to copy from.

- The template keeps its payload in `work/` and an agent-repo skeleton in `work.claude/`, two
  paths where `[family] template` names one.
- vc-x1's `agent-files diff` and `copy` fall back to `family.template`, so moving the key moves
  code.

#### Deliberation

- Home: vc-x1's `family/` directory holds the family's one copy (wink, 2026-10-16).
  - vc-x1 is already a member, every member runs its binary, and the code that reads the family
    lives beside it, so a schema change and the data it reads land in one cycle.
  - Weighed and left: the messages repo, drafted first, whose README version would then track two
    unrelated things, and a dedicated `vc-x1-family` repo, one more repo to clone and sync for two
    files.
  - Stable on every branch: `family/` changes only in a cycle of its own, which lands atomically,
    and every in-flight bookmark is then rebased onto the new `main`. A limit on vc-x1's own work,
    recorded in its `custom.md`.
- Shape: `family/family.md` holds `[resources]` and `[members]`, its paths relative to itself, and
  a member's `.vc-config.md` keeps `[family] member` and `home`, the path to `family/`.
  - The template's one key splits into `work-template` and `agent-template`, after its two
    payloads, and `messages` joins them as a resource.
  - `[members]` maps each member's name to its repo, so a member whose name is not its directory's,
    the template's `template`, is recorded rather than assumed.
- Copied, not pointed at: `family/custom.md` is the master, a member's `custom.md` begins with it
  verbatim and adds its own entries after, and a re-sync is a copy (wink, 2026-10-16).
  - It is how the agent-files already travel from the template's payload, so a member's rules stand
    on their own, and a diff against the master shows what the member added.
- Scope: vc-x1 and the family directory only. The template, iiac-perf, and zc-ring-x1 each adopt
  it themselves, the template next.
- Fast validation: `[validate] fast` becomes `cargo test --bins`, wink's call, ending the trial that
  made it the full list, so fast is fast again and clippy and the integration tests wait for the
  full run. It rides with the config rung, being the same file.
- Waiver: wink's go after the opening's work review covers the cycle through the closing's push,
  every rung's work and description reviews and every push included, so the agent runs the ladder
  without stopping (wink, 2026-10-16).
  - It does not cover Land, which waits for wink's review of the finished bookmark.
  - A deviation from the agreed plan or a question still stops the cycle ([Stop and
    ask](AGENTS.md#stop-and-ask)).
- Close-out shape: trapezoid, wink's choice at the opening.

#### Solution

Add `family/`, holding `family.md` and the master `custom.md`, teach vc-x1 to find the family
through `[family] home` and read its resources and members from `family.md`, switch vc-x1's own
config to it, and make vc-x1's `custom.md` the master followed by vc-x1's own entries.

#### Acceptance check

- `vc-x1 validate-config` passes on vc-x1's config, whose `[family]` holds `member` and `home`
  alone.
- `vc-x1 agent-files diff` with no directory compares against `../vc-x1-template/work`, found
  through `family/family.md`.
- vc-x1's `custom.md` begins with `family/custom.md` verbatim.
- `vc-x1 validate` passes.

- [feat: add the family directory][2] (done)
- [feat: config finds the family directory by home][3] (current)
- [docs: custom.md follows the family directory][4]

The cycle's setup commit: write this block, bump the version-of-record, and rename the package to
its dev name.

##### feat: add the family directory

The family has no one place to live. `family/family.md` holds its resources and members, and
`family/custom.md` the master every member's `custom.md` copies.

- `family.md` is a markdown file carrying toml blocks, the `.vc-config.md` format, so one reader
  serves both, and its prose states the directory's rule where every member reading it sees it.
- Paths are relative to `family/`, so each starts `../../` and names the sibling directly, the
  member's own entry included, `vc-x1 = "../../vc-x1"`.
- The master `custom.md` is vc-x1's as it stood on `main`, the Messaging and Fetch entries
  word for word what iiac-perf and zc-ring-x1 already carry, so adopting it changes nothing for
  them. Its `../vc-x1-messages` is relative to a member's root, where each copy lives, not to
  `family/`.
- Nothing reads the directory yet. The next rung teaches vc-x1 to.

vc-x1 reads `family.template` and `family.messages` from each member's own config. It follows
`[family] home` to `family.md` instead, and vc-x1's own config switches to it.

entry states the family directory's rule.

The config rung touches `README.md`, whose prose holds 13 semicolons, owed once touched

##### feat: the family directory closing

Closing out the cycle.

Add `family/`, holding `family.md` and the master `custom.md`, teach vc-x1 to find the family
through `[family] home` and read its resources and members from `family.md`, switch vc-x1's own
config to it, and make vc-x1's `custom.md` the master followed by vc-x1's own entries.

  alone.

  through `family/family.md`.

- `vc-x1 validate` passes.

##### feat: the family directory opening

The cycle's setup commit: write this block, bump the version-of-record, and rename the package to
its dev name.

##### feat: add the family directory

The family has no one place to live. `family/family.md` holds its resources and members, and
`family/custom.md` the master every member's `custom.md` copies.

- `family.md` is a markdown file carrying toml blocks, the `.vc-config.md` format, so one reader
  serves both, and its prose states the directory's rule where every member reading it sees it.
- Paths are relative to `family/`, so each starts `../../` and names the sibling directly, the
  member's own entry included, `vc-x1 = "../../vc-x1"`.
- The master `custom.md` is vc-x1's as it stood on `main`, the Messaging and Fetch entries
  word for word what iiac-perf and zc-ring-x1 already carry, so adopting it changes nothing for
  them. Its `../vc-x1-messages` is relative to a member's root, where each copy lives, not to
  `family/`.
- Nothing reads the directory yet. The next rung teaches vc-x1 to.

##### feat: config finds the family directory by home

vc-x1 reads `family.template` and `family.messages` from each member's own config. It follows
`[family] home` to `family.md` instead, and vc-x1's own config switches to it.

- `Family` in `src/family.rs` is the one reader: it follows the member's `home` to `family.md`,
  loads it with the config carrier's own loader, and answers a resource by name. A home without a
  `family.md` is an error, and no home is no family.
- A resource carries two forms of one place: the path, resolved against the family directory, for
  use, and the same place written from the member's config directory and normalized for a report,
  so `family/../../vc-x1-template/work` reads `../vc-x1-template/work`, as the old key's did.
- `agent-files diff` and `copy` fall back to the family's `work-template`, already resolved, so
  `resolve_set_dir` takes a resource where it took a string to resolve against the config's
  directory.
- The schema drops `family.template` and `family.messages` and gains `family.home`. Nothing read
  `family.messages` in code, its readers being the agent-files' prose and the Todo entries that
  plan to, which now name the family's `messages` resource.
- `family.md`'s tables are not in the schema, and `validate-config` does not open it. A family
  file that names an unknown resource or a member that is gone goes unreported until something
  reads it.
- `[members]` has no reader yet. It is data for the tools to come, `sync` fetching a family's
  repos and `vc-x1 msg`.
- The `family.member` doc no longer calls the name the member's record file in the messages repo,
  a file that went with the messages repo's v0.3.0.
- vc-x1's `.vc-config.md` takes wink's simplification with it: the prose shortened, the
  references dropped, and `fast` back to `cargo test --bins`.

##### docs: custom.md follows the family directory

vc-x1's `custom.md` has no master. It begins with `family/custom.md` verbatim, and its own first
entry states the family directory's rule.

##### docs: README prose loses its semicolons

The config rung touches `README.md`, whose prose holds 13 semicolons, owed once touched
([Semicolons](agent-data/prose.md#semicolons)).

##### feat: the family directory closing

Closing out the cycle.

# Doing: the cycle record

What is being done: the running cycle's planning and its work's documentation. The last
finished cycle's is in [zCLOSED.md](zCLOSED.md), and what we might do is in [TODO.md](TODO.md). The
block's shape is on trial: it opens with the Todo as it was picked from `TODO.md`, then the
Deliberation, the plan, Solution and Acceptance check, and the Ladder with its details.

This file is a trial (2026-10-09). The agent-files still name `TODO.md > ## In Progress` as the
record's home, and the cycle that makes this file the rule is [The cycle-record moves out of
TODO.md into zDOING.md](TODO.md#the-cycle-record-moves-out-of-todomd-into-zdoingmd).

## Continuation notes

Where the agent was, for the agent that comes next. Ephemeral, never a record: read first, acted
on, and reset to `_None._` by the reader. Kept here by the trial and no longer in `TODO.md`,
where [Acquaint](AGENTS.md#acquaint) still says to look.

_None._

## In Progress

### feat: the family directory

(wink + agent, 2026-10-16) Each member's `.vc-config.md` names the family's shared resources, the
template's payload and the messages repo, in a `[family]` table of its own, and nothing lists the
members, so the family's shape is copied into every member and drifts as members join, which is
coming soon. The shared part of each member's `custom.md`, its Messaging and Fetch entries, is
copied the same way, with no master to copy from.

- The template keeps its payload in `work/` and an agent-repo skeleton in `work.claude/`, two
  paths where `[family] template` names one.
- vc-x1's `agent-files diff` and `copy` fall back to `family.template`, so moving the key moves
  code.

#### Deliberation

- Home: vc-x1's `family/` directory holds the family's one copy (wink, 2026-10-16).
  - vc-x1 is already a member, every member runs its binary, and the code that reads the family
    lives beside it, so a schema change and the data it reads land in one cycle.
  - Weighed and left: the messages repo, drafted first, whose README version would then track two
    unrelated things, and a dedicated `vc-x1-family` repo, one more repo to clone and sync for two
    files.
  - Stable on every branch: `family/` changes only in a cycle of its own, which lands atomically,
    and every in-flight bookmark is then rebased onto the new `main`. A limit on vc-x1's own work,
    recorded in its `custom.md`.
- Shape: `family/family.md` holds `[resources]` and `[members]`, its paths relative to itself, and
  a member's `.vc-config.md` keeps `[family] member` and `home`, the path to `family/`.
  - The template's one key splits into `work-template` and `agent-template`, after its two
    payloads, and `messages` joins them as a resource.
  - `[members]` maps each member's name to its repo, so a member whose name is not its directory's,
    the template's `template`, is recorded rather than assumed.
- Copied, not pointed at: `family/custom.md` is the master, a member's `custom.md` begins with it
  verbatim and adds its own entries after, and a re-sync is a copy (wink, 2026-10-16).
  - It is how the agent-files already travel from the template's payload, so a member's rules stand
    on their own, and a diff against the master shows what the member added.
- Scope: vc-x1 and the family directory only. The template, iiac-perf, and zc-ring-x1 each adopt
  it themselves, the template next.
- Fast validation: `[validate] fast` becomes `cargo test --bins`, wink's call, ending the trial that
  made it the full list, so fast is fast again and clippy and the integration tests wait for the
  full run. It rides with the config rung, being the same file.
- Waiver: wink's go after the opening's work review covers the cycle through the closing's push,
  every rung's work and description reviews and every push included, so the agent runs the ladder
  without stopping (wink, 2026-10-16).
  - It does not cover Land, which waits for wink's review of the finished bookmark.
  - A deviation from the agreed plan or a question still stops the cycle ([Stop and
    ask](AGENTS.md#stop-and-ask)).
- Close-out shape: trapezoid, wink's choice at the opening.

#### Solution

Add `family/`, holding `family.md` and the master `custom.md`, teach vc-x1 to find the family
through `[family] home` and read its resources and members from `family.md`, switch vc-x1's own
config to it, and make vc-x1's `custom.md` the master followed by vc-x1's own entries.

#### Acceptance check

- `vc-x1 validate-config` passes on vc-x1's config, whose `[family]` holds `member` and `home`
  alone.
- `vc-x1 agent-files diff` with no directory compares against `../vc-x1-template/work`, found
  through `family/family.md`.
- vc-x1's `custom.md` begins with `family/custom.md` verbatim.
- `vc-x1 validate` passes.

##### feat: the family directory opening

The cycle's setup commit: write this block, bump the version-of-record, and rename the package to
its dev name.

##### feat: add the family directory

The family has no one place to live. `family/family.md` holds its resources and members, and
`family/custom.md` the master every member's `custom.md` copies.

- `family.md` is a markdown file carrying toml blocks, the `.vc-config.md` format, so one reader
  serves both, and its prose states the directory's rule where every member reading it sees it.
- Paths are relative to `family/`, so each starts `../../` and names the sibling directly, the
  member's own entry included, `vc-x1 = "../../vc-x1"`.
- The master `custom.md` is vc-x1's as it stood on `main`, the Messaging and Fetch entries
  word for word what iiac-perf and zc-ring-x1 already carry, so adopting it changes nothing for
  them. Its `../vc-x1-messages` is relative to a member's root, where each copy lives, not to
  `family/`.
- Nothing reads the directory yet. The next rung teaches vc-x1 to.

##### feat: config finds the family directory by home

vc-x1 reads `family.template` and `family.messages` from each member's own config. It follows
`[family] home` to `family.md` instead, and vc-x1's own config switches to it.

- `Family` in `src/family.rs` is the one reader: it follows the member's `home` to `family.md`,
  loads it with the config carrier's own loader, and answers a resource by name. A home without a
  `family.md` is an error, and no home is no family.
- A resource carries two forms of one place: the path, resolved against the family directory, for
  use, and the same place written from the member's config directory and normalized for a report,
  so `family/../../vc-x1-template/work` reads `../vc-x1-template/work`, as the old key's did.
- `agent-files diff` and `copy` fall back to the family's `work-template`, already resolved, so
  `resolve_set_dir` takes a resource where it took a string to resolve against the config's
  directory.
- The schema drops `family.template` and `family.messages` and gains `family.home`. Nothing read
  `family.messages` in code, its readers being the agent-files' prose and the Todo entries that
  plan to, which now name the family's `messages` resource.
- `family.md`'s tables are not in the schema, and `validate-config` does not open it. A family
  file that names an unknown resource or a member that is gone goes unreported until something
  reads it.
- `[members]` has no reader yet. It is data for the tools to come, `sync` fetching a family's
  repos and `vc-x1 msg`.
- The `family.member` doc no longer calls the name the member's record file in the messages repo,
  a file that went with the messages repo's v0.3.0.
- vc-x1's `.vc-config.md` takes wink's simplification with it: the prose shortened, the
  references dropped, and `fast` back to `cargo test --bins`.

##### docs: custom.md follows the family directory

vc-x1's `custom.md` has no master. It begins with `family/custom.md` verbatim, and its own first
entry states the family directory's rule.

##### docs: README prose loses its semicolons

The config rung touches `README.md`, whose prose holds 13 semicolons, and `src/agent_files.rs`,
whose comments hold one, owed once touched ([Semicolons](agent-data/prose.md#semicolons)).

##### feat: the family directory closing

Closing out the cycle.

and vc-x1's custom.md is a copy of it, so the boundary between the
family's entries and vc-x1's own needs saying, as does the rule the
directory puts on vc-x1, its host.

* Nothing in custom.md marks where the master's entries end.
  - A line after them names the master they came from and says vc-x1's
    own follow, so a re-sync copies up to it.
* The family directory's rule binds vc-x1, its host, alone.
  - vc-x1's first own entry states it: the directory changes only in a
    cycle of its own, every in-flight bookmark is then rebased onto the
    new main, and no other cycle's bookmark edits it."
input.description: Commit and push the custom.md rung in both repos
